units: Gitt. IV, 5 עוֹבֵד את רבו וכ׳ works one day for his master, and one for himself; a. fr. Esp. to do priestly service.
<cite ref="Chullin 24b:8">Ḥull. 24ᵇ</cite> <he>אחיו הכהנים … לַעֲבוֹד וכ׳</he> his brother priests allow him not to serve, until he is twenty years of age.

senses.gloss: to prepare; to till the ground; to dress (hides).
units: Gen. R. s. 22 קין עובד אדמה Cain the tiller of the ground. Y. Ab. Zar. II, 41ᵇ bot. גוי עוֹבְדָן; Tosef. ib. IV (V), 10 עוֹבְדוֹ, v. דָּבַב I; (Bab. ib. 33ᵃ עיבדן). Y. Sabb. I, 4ᵇ top נתן כלים … ומצאו עובד בו וכ׳ if one gave a gentile garments to wash, and found him working at them on the Sabbath; a. fr.—Part. pass. עָבוּד, pl. עֲבוּדִין dressed, v. infra.

senses.gloss: (v. עֲבוֹדָה) to use esp. for idolatrous purposes; to worship.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 3:7">Ab. Zar. III, 7</cite> (defining <he>אשרה</he>) <he>כל שעוֹבְדִין אותה</he> a tree which is itself worshipped (not one at which idolatrous rites are performed).
<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 3:7">Ib.</cite> <he>הואיל … הן עובדין</he> since they worship merely the image (under the tree).
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 7:6">Snh. VII, 6</cite> <he>העובד ע״ז אחד העובד וכ׳</he> he who worships an idol, whether he goes through the regular forms of that particular worship (v.

<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 3:5">Ab. Zar. III, 5</cite> <he>העכומ״ז העובדין וכ׳</he> as to idolaters that worship mountains and hills (as deities), they (the territories) may be used, but what is on them is forbidden.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 45b:1">Ib. 45ᵇ</cite> <he>אילן … ולבסוף עֲבָדוֹ</he> if one planted a tree and afterwards made it a subject of worship.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 46a:4">Ib. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>ועוֹבְדֵיהֶן בסייף</he> and those (Jews) who worship them are put to death by the sword; <cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 6:2">Tosef. ib. VI</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 7:8">VII</cite>), 8.

<cite ref="Shabbat 56b:4">Sabb. 56ᵇ</cite> <he>אילמלי לא … ולא עָבְדוּ ישראל ע״א</he> had David not listened to evil gossip (against Mephibosheth), … Israel would not have worshipped idols (under Jeroboam).
<cite ref="Shabbat 105b:8">Ib. 105ᵇ</cite> <he>עד שיאמר לו עֲבוֹד ע״ז</he> until he (the tempter) finally tells him, worship idols; <cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 9:31">Tosef. B. Kam. IX, 31</cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 13b:4">Ḥull. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>נכרים שבח״ל לאו עוֹבְדֵי ע״א הן</he> gentiles outside of Palestine must not be considered as idolaters; a. v. fr.

senses.gloss: to be prepared, dressed. Tosef. B. Kam. l. c. עורות שאינן נֶעֱבָדִין ed. Zuck. (oth. ed. עֲבוּדִין) undressed hides; a. e.

to be used, esp. for illicit purposes; to be worshipped. Tem. l. c. המוקצה והנ׳ the animal designated for idolatrous purposes and the one used; expl. כל שעובדין אותו whatever they may use it for ((e.g. yoking the ox, shearing the sheep for the benefit of idolatrous temples). Ib. 28ᵃ נעבדה בהן עבירה an illicit act has been done with them (by coupling them); ib. לא נֵתְעַבְּדָה בה עבירה no sinful act has been done with it (by which to unfit it for the altar).
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 46b:1">Ab. Zar. 46ᵇ</cite> <he>יש נ׳ במחובר אצל גבוה</he> does the law forbidding the use in divine worship of objects which have been used for idolatrous purposes include things fixed in the ground? <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 46b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>יש שינוי בנ׳</he> does change of form restore to legitimate use objects otherwise forbidden on account of their use in connection with idolatry? a. fr.
<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 162:6">Yalk. Ex. 162</cite> <he>הֶעֱבִידוֹ בכל וכ׳</he> he (Esau) oppressed him with all sorts of troubles.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 7:2">Sabb. VII, 2</cite> (among the labors forbidden on the Sabbath) <he>והמְעַבֵּד את עורו</he> dressing the hide of the deer (to fit it for parchment). Ib. 75ᵇ <he>חייב משום מעבד</he> is guilty of a Sabbath offence coming under the category of tanning.
<cite ref="Gittin 54b:19">Gitt. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>גוילין</he> … <he>לא עִיבַּדְתִּין לשמן</he> I did not prepare the parchment sheets with the proper intention; a. fr.
